newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline falls but cargo activity picks up.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline falls but cargo activity picks up.

text.p: NWE gasoline edged lower on Monday but traders said the cargo market was showing signs of life and keeping local supply on the snug side.
Eurograde barges fell $3 to $216/$218 fob ARA after a sharp selloff in crude late Friday and modest declines on Monday. The last trade heard was $216.50 fob.
In the cargo market, the arbitrage to the U.S. was still working for some sellers, traders said, despite the high freight rates and a drop in NYMEX gasoline futures.
A 60,000 tonne cargo of finished gasoline was confirmed sold last week for mid-February delivery into the U.S.
"There is marginal tightness in NWE," said one trader, adding it was still economical for some refiners to sell gasoline to the U.S. market.
Premium unleaded cargoes were notionally assessed at $222/$224 cif for Northwest Europe.
"The cargo market is starting to pick up," a broker said. "A lot of refiners in ARA are pretty balanced but are looking to put together parcels...to send to the U.S."
Further east, a 5,000 tonne parcel of Eurograde was sold last week into Riga for February 5-9 delivery, he said.
He also said Polish demand was quiet and would likely remain so until at least mid-February, despite renewed strike threats at Poland's second largest refinery, Gdansk.
A union official said on Monday that workers will hold a one-hour warning strike on Wednesday to press for shares in the company and a pay rise.
But the official said production at the 60,000 barrel per day refinery would not be halted.
